title: Plan a brand's AI media rollout: content credentials, labels, review and limits
scenario: A camping brand will launch an AI-made campaign on Friday at 10:00. You set the credentials, the labels, the limits, the incident plan and the watching before it goes live. Use the exhibit. The brand, the files, the limits and the plan are made up for this case. The vendor and platform lines are copied from the pages.
exhibit:
BRIEF:
  Cedar & Stone, a camping brand. A three-week campaign on YouTube and TikTok.
  Assets: 40 hero images from Nano Banana 2.1; one realistic Veo 3.1 clip of a real
  national-park trail that nobody filmed; a site helper, "Ask Cedar". Launch Friday 10:00.

PARTNER FILE (made up for this case):
  P1  logo-lockup.png from a partner agency. Provenance check, c2pa entry:
      validation_state invalid, issuer none, outcome not_detected.
      The partner wants the caption "Content Credentials verified".

LIMITS for the image project (made up for this case):
  IPM 40 images per minute | RPD 1,000 requests per day. Each request makes 1 image.
  Day-one plan: 900 images spread evenly over the first 30 minutes, then 200 more in the afternoon. All times are Pacific time.

INCIDENT PLAN (ours, made up for this case):
  Row 1  Key leaked          Revoke the key, then replace it.                Owner: Priya
  Row 2  Wrong asset live    Find the cause first, then pause the ad.        Owner: "the team"
  Row 3  Retired tool        Read the vendors' deprecation pages monthly.    Owner: Priya

AFTER LAUNCH (made up for this case):
  Draft set-up: none, "because the 50-prompt test covered every case".

LINES (copied from the pages):
  OpenAI: "Don't treat an `invalid` manifest as reliable provenance evidence."
  YouTube: creators must disclose content that "Alters footage of a real event or place" or "Generates a realistic scene that didn't actually occur."
  TikTok (newsroom post, May 2024): it has "required creators to label realistic AIGC for over a year".
  Gemini: "Your usage is evaluated against each limit, and exceeding any of them will trigger a rate limit error."
  Google: "No matter how much you test and mitigate, you can never guarantee perfection, so plan upfront how you'll spot and deal with problems that arise."

questions.prompt: What do you say about the partner's caption for P1, "Content Credentials verified"?

options.text: Use it, because the file does carry a Content Credential from the partner agency itself
options.explanation: The check says the manifest is invalid. A credential that fails the check is not verified.

options.text: Hold it back and ask for the original file, because an invalid manifest is unreliable
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says not to treat an invalid manifest as reliable provenance evidence. The original file may still hold a good manifest.

options.text: Use it, because not_detected shows that the file holds no AI content at all
options.explanation: not_detected does not say anything about whether AI was used, and it does not mean verified.

options.text: Do not use it, because a file from another company can never carry credentials
options.explanation: Other companies can issue valid credentials. This file's manifest is the problem.

questions.prompt: What is the label plan for the Veo clip of the real trail?

options.text: Answer Yes to AI use on YouTube and label it as AI on TikTok, because both ask for it
options.explanation: Right. The clip is a realistic scene of a real place that never happened. YouTube requires disclosure, and TikTok said in May 2024 that it requires creators to label realistic AI content. Check its current page before launch.

options.text: Label it only on YouTube, because TikTok reads Content Credentials by itself
options.explanation: TikTok said it has required creators to label realistic AI content, and reading credentials does not replace that.

options.text: Skip both labels, because the clip is short and shows only a quiet trail
options.explanation: Length does not matter. A realistic scene that never happened needs disclosure.

options.text: Label it on TikTok only, because YouTube asks about music and not video
options.explanation: YouTube's list includes altering footage of a real place and realistic scenes that did not occur.

questions.prompt: What do the limits say about the day-one plan of 900 images in 30 minutes, then 200 more?

options.text: Everything fits, because the daily meter resets at noon, before the afternoon run
options.explanation: Gemini's daily quotas reset at midnight Pacific time, not at noon. 900 plus 200 is 1,100, more than 1,000.

options.text: It all works, because 30 images a minute is below the limit of 40 images a minute
options.explanation: The daily limit is a second meter. 1,100 requests are more than 1,000.

options.text: The morning fails, because 900 images in 30 minutes is really 45 images a minute
options.explanation: 900 divided by 30 is 30, not 45.

options.text: The morning fits, because 30 a minute is under 40, but 1,100 passes the daily 1,000
options.explanation: Right. 900 divided by 30 is 30 per minute, below 40. But 900 plus 200 is 1,100, and exceeding any one limit triggers an error.

questions.prompt: Which row of the incident plan should change first, and how?

options.text: Row 1: replace the key first and revoke it afterwards, so that the apps never stop
options.explanation: With a leak the harm is live. The plan is right to revoke first, then replace.

options.text: Row 3: read the deprecation pages only on the day a tool is shut down for good
options.explanation: A shutdown date is a deadline. The monthly reading, with a named owner, is the better plan.

options.text: Row 2: pause the ad and swap in the master, then find the cause and name an owner
options.explanation: Right. The five steps put contain before fix, and a row owned by "the team" has no one who acts.

options.text: Row 2: wait for the cause to be found before touching the ad, then name an owner
options.explanation: The ad keeps reaching people while the team looks for the cause.

questions.prompt: What should the brand set up for after launch, instead of "none"?

options.text: Nothing more, because the 50-prompt test covered every case before launch
options.explanation: Google says you can never guarantee perfection, so plan how you will spot problems.

options.text: A spend alert, a usage check, and a feedback channel that a named person reads
options.explanation: Right. Google says to plan upfront how you will spot problems, and to use a monitored channel. OpenAI suggests spend alerts and usage tracking.

options.text: Only a feedback inbox, checked whenever someone happens to have a free moment
options.explanation: A channel that nobody is named to read is not a plan, and it leaves out spend and usage.

options.text: Only a spend alert, because money is the one thing that can go wrong later
options.explanation: Wrong assets, misuse and shutdowns need a way to be spotted too.
